items.title: Tongan women 'auctioned off' for marriage in China
items.description: The ABC has spoken to multiple Tongan women who have been lured into an arranged marriage syndicate operating in China, with allegations of passports being confiscated and tens of thousands of dollars changing hands.

items.title: Ex-ASIO source denied visa to give evidence at Bondi royal commission
items.description: The man who previously warned ASIO about the Bondi gunmen will not be able to give sensitive and classified evidence at the Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

items.title: The 'fairy gold dust passport' more Australians are chasing
items.description: Australians are racing to secure Irish citizenship, with new figures showing applications have more than doubled in the past three years as people seek the right to live, work and study across the EU.

items.title: 'Nervous' investors retreat from housing market as downturn broadens
items.description: Australia's property market has entered a downturn after both house and unit prices fell for the first time in more than three years, bringing an end to the recent housing boom.

items.title: Labor powerbrokers cut AI deal for workers
items.description: Labor will respond to growing anxiety about the rise of artificial intelligence with a new taskforce to give Australian workers a greater say in how the technology shapes the nation.

items.title: Labor's members to debate gas and gambling
items.description: Anthony Albanese may have been a keen participant in robust conference debates in years gone by but is now using his authority to enforce a much more controlled process.

items.title: A student took to social media, now he's taking on one of the world's most powerful leaders
items.description: The student who started a youth uprising across India is fast becoming the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 12-year reign.

items.title: Live: Labor to extend paid placements to more care industry students
items.description: Anthony Albanese will announce an expansion of the Commonwealth's "paid prac" scheme at Labor's National Conference. Follow live.

items.title: Inside CPAC London: Charlatans, conspiracy theories and loud snoring
items.description: In 10 years at the ABC, I've had some strange experiences. I can now add last week's CPAC conference in London to the list, and it's going somewhere near the top, says Riley Stuart in London.

items.title: Breaking: US and Saudi Arabia reach nuclear cooperation deal
items.description: Israeli officials and US politicians from both parties have voiced concern that a civilian nuclear project in Saudi Arabia could be used to eventually develop nuclear weapons.

items.title: Trump threatens Iranian power plants, bridges if ships attacked in Hormuz
items.description: US strikes have already widened from the south to western and central areas of Iran in recent days.

items.title: How we got to Glasgow 2026 and what the Commonwealth Games will look like
items.description: The bumpy road to Glasgow 2026 has produced a Commonwealth Games that will look a little different than the ones that came before.

items.title: How vulnerable children end up in houses where abuse flourishes
items.description: The ABC has spoken with experts, advocates and residential care workers as part of a 19-month investigation into the sexual exploitation of children in state care.

items.title: Live: ASX set to open higher as Tesla shares plunge
items.description: The Australian share market is set to open in the green after Tesla shares plunging on cash flow news. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: How Nintendo's tariff hike ended with angry gamers and a lawsuit
items.description: Nintendo has argued it has no duty to pass its refunds onto US consumers. It's the latest in a lengthy tariff fight.

items.title: You reckon you know the Logies? Try our quiz
items.description: As the Logies approach, on August 16, we thought we would test your knowledge of the beloved but daggy Australian television awards and this year's nominees.

items.title: The nefarious rise of Putin is skewered in this satirical drama
items.description: Cannes darling Oliver Assayas tackles the shadowy forces of our time in his latest film, The Wizard of the Kremlin.

items.title: Rock Posters proud to capture artists' 'blood and tears' in billboards
items.description: The iconic Melbourne printing factory has worked with international pop divas and rock legends to enhance the city's live music scene for 40 years.

items.title: China demands Australia stop 'inciting confrontation' over South China Sea
items.description: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has demanded Australia stop "exaggerating tensions and inciting confrontation" over the South China Sea after Penny Wong warned Beijing against "destabilising" conduct in the region.

items.title: How One Nation's winning over the bush
items.description: One Nation has some of its strongest support in outback Australia and recent polling shows it could win over 30 regional seats. So what's winning over regional Australians when it comes to Pauline Hanson's party?

items.title: AFL's first publicly gay player calls for respect in Crows-Pies match
items.description: Four months after becoming the first current or former AFL player to publicly come out as gay, Leigh Ryswyk is urging fans not to boo the Collingwood player targeted by Crow Izak Rankine’s homophobic slur.

items.title: Rebel Wilson's victory in defamation case could be short-lived. Here's why
items.description: As lawyers for actor Charlotte MacInnes plan to appeal a failed defamation case outcome against Hollywood star Rebel Wilson, a solicitor says the judge's interpretations could be grounds for a retrial or a different verdict.

items.title: When Gordon Bray and his Homebush schoolmates ruled their rugby world
items.description: It may be more than 60 years ago, but Homebush Boys High's 1965 Waratah Shield win remains a fond memory for the likes of Gordon Bray, John Symond and John Coates.

items.title: Captain Cook Shopping Centre sold to Arnhem Land Aboriginal corporation
items.description: British explorer James Cook never visited Nhulunbuy on his voyages, but his namesake shopping complex stood there for decades — until now.

items.title: 'Land grab' concerns as developers invited to build in iconic NT parks
items.description: The Northern Territory government says opening up national parks to private investors will unlock their "tourism potential", but an expert fears the move could mean less access for locals and budget-conscious visitors.
